metadata.title: Subjective well-being and educational performance in PISA: A copula based approach

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2022 student questionnaire life-satisfaction item ST016 and a subset of countries that administered the additional well-being questionnaire, then constructs a latent SWB factor score via factor analysis. For the main copula analysis, the paper does not report applying PISA complex-sampling weights or any specific weight variable; it instead focuses on distribution fitting and copula dependence modeling. In the robustness check, the authors explicitly state a weighted least squares (WLS) regression using final adjusted student weight W_FSTUWT and they run the analysis in IEA IDB Analyzer 5.0 and SPSS 27. Because the copula modeling section does not describe weight usage, weighting appears to be applied only in the robustness regression, not in the copula dependence estimation.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The paper uses a single plausible value for PISA scores (PV1READ, PV1MATH, PV1SCIE) and does not describe any missing-data strategy for either the questionnaire items used to build the SWB factor scores or the PV inputs. This is a reporting gap because PISA microdata typically contain missingness in background and questionnaire items, and the factor-score construction would require a documented rule (e.g., complete cases or imputation) to ensure reproducibility. The absence of a stated missing-data approach limits confidence in the stability of the latent SWB construct and the dependence estimates.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The SWB construct is derived from the student life-satisfaction item ST016 plus selected well-being questionnaire items (WB155Q01, WB155Q08, WB155Q10). The authors restrict observations to countries/economies that administered the additional well-being questionnaire (13 countries/economies listed in the paper). For PISA performance, they merge PV1READ, PV1MATH, and PV1SCIE by taking the mean across the three to create a single overall PISA score per country, and they use only one plausible value as stated in the data preparation section.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 (15-year-olds) — overall performance (mean of PV1READ, PV1MATH, PV1SCIE) and latent SWB factor score from ST016 + WB155Q01/WB155Q08/WB155Q10
main_findings.target_variable: Dependence between PISA performance and SWB construct (copula dependence; Gaussian copula parameter)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Gaussian copula: parameter estimate θ = 0.005; Cramér–von Mises Sn = 3.816 (p=0.000); Scaillet test p=0.78; CIC indicates Gaussian best fit. Robustness: Pearson correlation r=0.026; WLS regression (Table A.1) reports small coefficients near zero for Math/Reading/Science across countries; overall model R2=0.030, p-value=0.000 (No. of observations=114,244).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2022 the study leveraged the SWB construct components (ST016 life satisfaction plus WB155Q01/WB155Q08/WB155Q10) to model the dependence between students’ overall PISA performance and latent SWB via copula functions, finding that the Gaussian copula parameter implies only weak positive dependence (θ=0.005) and that goodness-of-fit is mixed (Cramér–von Mises rejects, Scaillet does not). This indicates that improving academic performance alone is unlikely to substantially raise adolescent subjective well-being, so education policy should treat performance and well-being as related but largely separable targets, while noting the cross-sectional design and the lack of documented missing-data handling for the latent SWB factor.

data.outcome_summary: The paper analyzes PISA 2022 (15-year-olds) using a copula-based approach to study the dependence between overall educational performance and a latent subjective well-being (SWB) construct. The SWB construct is built from a factor analysis using ST016 life satisfaction plus well-being questionnaire items (WB155Q01, WB155Q08, WB155Q10), and the authors restrict the sample to the 13 countries/economies that administered the additional well-being questionnaire. For performance, they merge PV1READ, PV1MATH, and PV1SCIE by averaging them and they use only one plausible value. Across five copula families, the CIC criterion selects the Gaussian copula, yielding a very small dependence parameter (θ=0.005) and a weak Pearson correlation (r=0.026). A robustness check using WLS with W_FSTUWT in IEA IDB Analyzer reports small coefficients and low explanatory power (R2=0.030), but the copula section does not document missing-data handling or hierarchical dependence adjustments, limiting causal interpretation and reproducibility.
data.null_fields_interpretation: Although the study is empirical and uses PISA 2022 data, it does not train predictive machine-learning models; instead, it fits statistical copula dependence structures and performs a factor-analysis-based SWB construction. Consequently, the ML technique fields are intentionally left empty (no supervised ML algorithms are evaluated), and the main result is reported as dependence-structure parameters and goodness-of-fit statistics rather than ML predictive accuracy.
